gaps.sentence: Visitors ___ wear badges at all times inside the plant.
gaps.explanation: 'Must' = a rule that has to be followed.

gaps.sentence: Library books ___ be taken out of the reading room.
gaps.hint: a passive prohibition with mustn't be
gaps.explanation: Prohibitions can be passive: mustn't be taken.

gaps.sentence: The lights are on and I can hear the vacuum cleaner, so someone ___ be at home.
gaps.explanation: Evidence-based certainty uses 'must': must be at home.

gaps.sentence: You ___ have seen a ghost — there is no such thing!
gaps.hint: a past claim rejected as impossible
gaps.explanation: 'Can't have' rejects a past claim as impossible: can't have seen.

gaps.sentence: You ___ as well take the early train — the later one is often cancelled.
gaps.hint: might as well = no reason not to
gaps.explanation: 'Might as well' suggests an option because the alternative is worse.

gaps.sentence: ___ I use your phone for a local call?
She ___ to pass one more exam to qualify as an architect.
gaps.explanation: 'Need to' conjugates like a normal verb: she needs to pass.

gaps.sentence: There was plenty of food left, so the guests ___ have been hungry.
gaps.explanation: The evidence (leftover food) rules out hunger: can't have been.
